name: ContributionGraph
label: Contribution graph
description: A year of activity, one cell per day.

props.name: days
props.description: One entry per day, ordered oldest to newest

props.name: title
props.description:
Chart title, in the shared chart header.
Note: this replaces the native `title` tooltip attribute, which the graph does not expose.

props.name: bare
props.description: Strip the card chrome (border, padding, fill) when the chart sits inside another panel that supplies the surface

props.name: caption
props.description: Summary line shown under the grid, e.g. "496 contributions in the last year"

props.name: showMonthLabels
props.description: Show month labels above the grid

props.name: showLegend
props.description: Show the Less → More legend under the grid

props.name: gridLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the grid of day cells, which renders as one image. Falls back to `caption`, then to "Contribution activity".

props.name: lessLabel
props.description: The legend's low-end word. Defaults to "Less".

props.name: moreLabel
props.description: The legend's high-end word. Defaults to "More".

props.name: locale
props.description:
The BCP 47 locale the dates are written in: the default month labels
above the grid ("Jan" to "Dec" in `en-US`) and the date in each cell's
default tooltip ("Jul 8, 2026"), and the weekday each column starts on. Defaults to `en-US`.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.description:
The weekday each column starts on, 0 (Sunday) to 6 (Saturday). Defaults to
the first day of the week in `locale`: Sunday in `en-US`, Monday in `de-DE`.

props.name: monthLabels
props.description:
The month labels above the grid: twelve entries, January first.
Defaults to the short month names in `locale` ("Jan" to "Dec" in
`en-US`); a list of any other length falls back to the default.

props.name: cellLabel
props.description:
A day cell's tooltip, given its count and date. Defaults to "No
contributions", "1 contribution" or "N contributions", then "on" and the
date in `locale`'s short form (e.g. "Jul 8, 2026").
